plan: Store a deep copy of the input dict and treat it as a composite tree: workspace holds a list of items; section/group items hold nested item lists; note/reference items are leaves.
Implement total_word_count as a recursive fold: containers sum children, notes count \\b\\w+\\b words after blanking [[?id]] marker tokens, references contribute their declared word_count.
Implement unresolved_markers as a recursive traversal accumulating a set from note-text marker identifiers and reference unresolved lists, returned sorted lexicographically.
Implement outline as a deterministic preorder traversal emitting the workspace title, then '  '*level + '<kind>: <title>' per item, with top-level items at level 1.

Implement move with full up-front validation (string ids, item exists, destination exists and is a container or 'workspace', destination is not the item or inside its subtree, index in 0..len(dest)); only after all checks pass, delete from the source list and insert/append into the destination, so any failure leaves state untouched.
Implement to_data as a deep copy of the internal dict so external mutation can never corrupt the workspace.
mechanisms: composite tree of dicts with kind-based dispatch (containers: section/group; leaves: note/reference)
recursive aggregation fold for total word count with marker-stripped note text
set-accumulating recursive traversal for unresolved marker identifiers, sorted output
deterministic preorder traversal with two-spaces-per-level indentation for outline
containment invariant enforced by identity-based subtree membership check (no self/descendant destinations)
atomic validate-then-mutate move: all ValueError checks precede the single del+insert mutation
deep-copy isolation at construction and in to_data
